extracted.intended_audience: FOIA and Privacy Act requesters and agency FOIA/Privacy Act personnel (e.g., requesters, news-media, educational and research institutions, agency records officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and procedural requirements for submitting, processing, charging for, appealing, and preserving records responsive to FOIA and Privacy Act requests, including definitions of requester categories, fee rules, and consultation/referral procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decision timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on your appeal will be made in writing, ordinarily within 20 working days of receipt of your appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision affirming an adverse determination in whole or in part will contain a statement of the reason(s) for the affirmance, including any FOIA exemption(s) applied, and will inform you of the FOIA provisions for court review of the decision. If the adverse determination is reversed or modified on appeal, in whole or in part, then you will be notified in a written decision and your request will be reprocessed in accordance with that appeal decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in dispute resolution services (OGIS mediation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediation is a voluntary process conducted by OGIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency agrees to participate in the mediation services provided by OGIS, it will actively engage in the process in an attempt to resolve the dispute. Mediation is a non-exclusive alternative to FOIA litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to appeal before seeking court review
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, if you wish to seek review by a court of any adverse determination, you must first appeal it in a timely fashion under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to both FOIA and Privacy Act adverse determinations where the regulation specifies an administrative appeal is normally a prerequisite to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: General fee-charging rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will charge for processing requests under the FOIA in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section and with the OMB Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency ordinarily will collect all applicable fees before sending copies of requested records to a requester. Requesters must pay fees by check or money order made payable to the Treasury of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Commercial use request
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Commercial use request’ means a request from or on behalf of a person who seeks information for a use or purpose that furthers his or her commercial, trade, or profit interests, including furthering those interests through litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will determine, whenever reasonably possible, the use to which a requester will put the requested records and may seek clarification when it appears the requester will put records to a commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Direct costs’ means those expenses that an agency actually incurs in searching for and duplicating (and, in the case of commercial use requests, reviewing) records to respond to a FOIA request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct costs include, for example, salary of the employee performing the work (basic rate plus 16 percent to cover benefits) and cost of operating duplication machinery. Overhead such as space, heating, or lighting is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Duplication’ means the making of a copy of a record, or of the information contained in it, necessary to respond to a FOIA request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies can be paper, audiovisual, or electronic. The agency will honor a requester’s specified preference of form or format if the record is readily reproducible with reasonable efforts in that form or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Educational institution
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Educational institution’ means a preschool, elementary or secondary school, institution of undergraduate, graduate, professional, or vocational higher education that operates a program of scholarly research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify, requester must show the request is authorized by and made under the auspices of the institution and that records are sought to further scholarly research, not for commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Noncommercial scientific institution
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Noncommercial scientific institution’ means an institution not operated on a commercial basis and operated solely for conducting scientific research the results of which are not intended to promote any particular product or industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify, requester must show the request is authorized by and made under the auspices of the institution and that records are sought to further scientific research, not commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Representative of the news media
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Representative of the news media’ means any person or entity that gathers information of potential interest to a segment of the public, uses editorial skills to turn raw materials into a distinct work, and distributes that work to an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News means information about current events or of current public interest. Examples include broadcasters and publishers (if they disseminate news). Freelance journalists qualify if they can demonstrate a solid basis for expecting publication (e.g., a publication contract or past publication record). Request must not be for commercial use; requests supporting news-dissemination are not considered commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Review (record examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Review’ means the examination of a record located in response to a request to determine whether any portion is exempt from disclosure and includes processing the record for disclosure (e.g., redaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review costs are recoverable even if a record is ultimately not disclosed. Review time includes time spent considering formal objections by business submitters under § 304.7, but does not include time resolving general legal or policy issues regarding exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Search (for responsive records)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Search’ means the process of looking for and retrieving records or information responsive to a request, including page-by-page or line-by-line identification and reasonable efforts to locate electronic records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency will conduct searches in the most efficient and least expensive manner reasonably possible (e.g., not searching line-by-line when duplicating an entire document would be quicker and less expensive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fees: who is charged and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fees will be charged for all requests (other than requests made by educational institutions, noncommercial scientific institutions, or representatives of the news media) subject to paragraph (d) limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may charge for time spent searching even if no responsive record is located or if located records are withheld. Rates: $5.00 per quarter hour for clerical personnel; $10.00 per quarter hour for professional personnel; $15.00 per quarter hour for managerial personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer search charges
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer searches of records, requesters will be charged the direct costs of conducting the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain requesters will be charged no search fee and some will be entitled to the cost equivalent of two hours of manual search time without charge. Direct costs include operator/programmer salary apportionable to the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication fees will be charged to all requesters, subject to paragraph (d) limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper photocopy fee is ten cents per page (no more than one copy supplied). For computer-produced copies (tapes, disks, printouts), agency will charge direct costs including operator time. For other forms of duplication, direct costs of that duplication will be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review fees for commercial requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Review fees will be charged to requesters who make a commercial use request for the initial record review when the agency determines whether an exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No charge for review at the administrative appeal level regarding an exemption already applied. Records withheld under an exemption that is later found not to apply may be reviewed again and that review's costs are chargeable. Review fees charged at same rates as search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on charging fees (general exemptions and free allowances)
rubrics_metrics.description: No search fee will be charged for requests by educational institutions, noncommercial scientific institutions, or representatives of the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No search or review fee will be charged for a quarter-hour period unless more than half that period is required. Except for commercial-use requesters, the agency will provide without charge the first 100 pages of duplication (or cost equivalent) and the first two hours of search (or cost equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee when total fees are $20 or less
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a total fee calculated under paragraph (c) is $20.00 or less for any request, no fee will be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs (d)(3) and (d)(4) work together so that for non-commercial requesters no fee will be charged unless the cost of search in excess of two hours plus cost of duplication in excess of 100 pages totals more than $20.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee consequences when agency misses statutory time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency fails to comply with the FOIA’s time limits to respond, it may not charge search fees, or, for certain requesters, duplication fees, except as described in subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include timely written notice for unusual circumstances (allowing additional 10 working days) or where unusual circumstances and more than 5,000 pages are necessary: agency must provide timely notice, discuss scope-limiting with requester (or make three good-faith attempts) before charging. Court-ordered exceptional circumstances are handled per order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for anticipated fees over $50
rubrics_metrics.description: When the agency determines or estimates that fees will amount to more than $50.00, it will notify the requester of the actual or estimated amount of the fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a portion can be estimated, the agency will advise the requester that the estimated fee might be only a portion of the total. The request will not be considered received and further work will not be done until requester agrees to pay. Notice should offer opportunity to discuss reformulation to lower cost; if requester previously indicated a willingness to pay a lesser amount, processing may be suspended pending response.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Public Liaison assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will make its FOIA Public Liaison available to assist any requester in reformulating a request to meet needs at a lower cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as part of the notice/fee-estimate process to help reduce fees by narrowing scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges for other special services
rubrics_metrics.description: When the agency chooses as administrative discretion to provide a special service (e.g., certifying that records are true copies or sending by other than ordinary mail), the direct costs of providing the service ordinarily will be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These charges are separate from the fee schedule in paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging interest on unpaid bills
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may charge interest on any unpaid bill starting on the 31st day following the date of billing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest assessed at the rate provided in 31 U.S.C. 3717 and will accrue from the date of billing until payment is received. Agency will follow the Debt Collection Act provisions and applicable regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating requests to prevent fee avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the agency reasonably believes a requester or group is attempting to divide a request into a series to avoid fees, it may aggregate those requests and charge accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will presume multiple requests of this type within a 30-day period have been made to avoid fees. Requests separated by a longer period will be aggregated only if solid basis exists. Multiple requests involving unrelated matters will not be aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payments when fees exceed thresholds or prior nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency will not require advance payment for most requests, except where the agency determines or estimates a total fee will be more than $250.00 it may require advance payment up to the entire anticipated fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: satisfactory assurance of full payment from a requester with a prompt payment history can avoid advance payment. If requester previously failed to pay properly charged FOIA fees within 30 calendar days, agency may require full payment plus interest and advance payment of anticipated fee before processing new or pending requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees charged under other statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee schedule of this section does not apply to fees charged under any statute that specifically requires an agency to set and collect fees for particular types of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where responsive records are maintained for distribution by another agency under a statutory fee schedule, ACUS will inform requesters of steps to obtain records from those sources to do so most economically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for waiver or reduction of fees (public interest test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters may seek a waiver of fees by submitting a written application demonstrating disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will grant waiver/reduction when all factors in (k)(2)(i)-(iii) are satisfied: (i) disclosure would shed light on identifiable government operations with a direct and clear connection; (ii) disclosure is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding, satisfied when (A) it is meaningfully informative (not already public) and (B) it contributes to understanding of a reasonably broad audience (news media presumed to satisfy); (iii) disclosure is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester — agency considers whether requester has a commercial interest and whether that is the primary interest furthered. Partial waivers possible for portion of records; waivers should ordinarily be requested with the initial request but can be submitted later while the request is pending or on appeal. If requester committed to pay fees and later requests waiver that is denied, requester must pay costs incurred up to date waiver request was received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of records
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will preserve all correspondence pertaining to the requests that it receives under this subpart, as well as copies of all requested records, until disposition or destruction is authorized by title 44 or NARA's General Records Schedule 4.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records will not be disposed of while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, or lawsuit under the FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of contracted records maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency contracts with another agency, entity, or person to maintain records for record management purposes, it will promptly identify such records in its 'Freedom of Information Reference Guide' and specify how requests for such records can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures requesters know where and how to request records maintained by contractors or other agencies on behalf of ACUS.

rubrics_metrics.name: No entitlement beyond FOIA/Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this subpart shall be construed to entitle any person, as of right, to any service or to the disclosure of any record to which such person is not entitled under the FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that procedures do not create additional disclosure rights beyond statutory entitlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of Privacy Act rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules in this subpart contain the procedures ACUS follows under the Privacy Act regarding protection of, and individual access to, certain records about individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules apply to all records in Privacy Act systems of records maintained by the agency which are retrieved by an individual's name or personal identifier. They should be read together with the Privacy Act; Privacy Act requests are processed under FOIA rules and are subject only to exemptions applicable under both FOIA and the Privacy Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act: request methods and addressing
rubrics_metrics.description: You may make a request for access to a record about yourself by appearing in person or by sending an e-mail addressed to info@acus.gov, mail to the specified address, or by fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For quickest handling of a mail request, mark both the request letter and the envelope 'Privacy Act Request.' Fax number and physical mailing address are provided in the regulation text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act: description of records sought
rubrics_metrics.description: You must describe the records you want in enough detail to enable agency personnel to locate the system of records containing them with a reasonable amount of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible, include description of records sought, time periods they were compiled, and name or identifying number of each system of records. The agency publishes a FEDERAL REGISTER notice describing its systems of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act: agreement to pay fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A Privacy Act request for access to records will be considered an agreement by you to pay all applicable fees charged under § 304.27, up to $50.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplication fees in excess of $50 are subject to § 304.27 and notification requirements in § 304.9. The agency ordinarily will confirm this agreement in an acknowledgment letter. Requester may specify willingness to pay a greater or lesser amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act: verification of identity
rubrics_metrics.description: When you make a request for access to records about yourself, you must verify your identity by stating full name, current address, and date/place of birth and signing the request with a notarized signature or a signature submitted under 28 U.S.C. 1746.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the last four digits of your social security number is optional but may help identification and location of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for responding and scope of included records
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will be responsible for responding to a request in all respects, except when referral to another agency is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining responsive records, the agency ordinarily will include only records in its possession and control as of the date it begins its search. If any other date is used, the agency will inform the requester of that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations and referrals for Privacy Act requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When the agency receives a request for a record, it will determine whether another agency is better able to determine whether the record is exempt from access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency is best able, it will process after consulting with the other agency; if not, it will either respond after consultation or refer responsibility to the agency best able (often the originating agency). The agency ordinarily presumes the originating agency is best able.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and timing for referrals and consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the agency refers all or part of the responsibility for responding to another agency, it ordinarily will notify the requester and inform the requester of the name of the agency and the part referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All consultations and referrals will be handled according to the date upon which the Privacy Act access request was initially received by the first agency, not any later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements to streamline consultations/referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may make agreements with other agencies designed to eliminate the need for consultations or referrals for particular types of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such agreements can speed processing for commonly-shared or jointly-managed records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of Privacy Act requests
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of a request, the agency ordinarily will send an acknowledgment letter confirming the requester’s agreement to pay fees under § 304.21(c) and provide an assigned request number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases the agency may seek further information or clarification from the requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of access procedure under Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the agency determines to grant access in whole or in part, it will notify the requester in writing, inform of any fee charged, and will disclose records promptly on payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested in person, agency may disclose records directly if not unreasonably disruptive; a written record of the grant should be made. If requester is accompanied by another person, written authorization is required before discussing records in presence of the other person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse determination content for Privacy Act requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon making an adverse determination denying a request for access in any respect, the agency will notify the requester in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include (1) the name and title/position of the person responsible for the denial; (2) a brief statement of the reason(s) for the denial, including any Privacy Act exemption(s) applied; and (3) a statement that the denial may be appealed under § 304.24(a) with a description of the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing requirements for Privacy Act denials
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied, you may appeal an adverse determination to the Chairman; appeal must be in writing by e-mail or letter and received within 60 days of the date of the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal should provide reasons and supporting information, clearly identify the particular determination (including request number), and for mail appeals mark letter and envelope 'Privacy Act Appeal.' The Chairman or designee will act on the appeal except ordinarily when request becomes subject of FOIA/Privacy Act litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal response content and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on your appeal will be made in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision affirming an adverse determination will include reasons and any exemption applied and inform of Privacy Act provisions for court review. If reversed or modified, requester will be notified in writing and request will be reprocessed in accordance with appeal decision.
